phase: 9B.1A — Supabase preview activation and live account certification

items.evidence: Live on the durable origin: the header drops both account prompts for an identity chip, and the chip opens a menu offering My EraClash, Account settings and Sign out. Signing out returns the header to Sign in and Create free account with guest play intact.

Live, with two isolated browser contexts: a Clash saved on the first device is read back on the second by RESULT ID, not merely by count, and a third context signed in as a different account sees none of them.

reason: A live Supabase session and cloud database did not exist when Phase 9B.1 ran. The capabilities were not unreproducible; they were not yet live-testable. The distinction matters because one implies a defect that could not be pinned down and the other implies a dependency that had not been supplied.
currentState: Both ledger items are FIXED_AND_VERIFIED. Reaching that state also required a deployment fault to be corrected: the Preview-scoped SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY had never been updated, so every cloud write returned 401 while every static check reported the system ready.
note: data/validation/9b1/* is left exactly as recorded. This file is the correction kept beside it. No item has been marked verified on the strength of a code path alone.

defects: exchangeCodeForSession was handed a URL where its parameter is an auth code, so no click could ever complete a sign-in
the paste field stripped every non-digit, so the only proof the default email template sends could not be entered
a pkce_-prefixed token was redeemed as a raw token, which hashes it twice and always fails
the address-bar scrub erased the SDK's sb_flow_id before the exchange read it, so an older link presented the newer link's verifier
PKCE bound an emailed link to the browser that requested it, which a mail app almost never is; the email flow is now implicit
Supabase Site URL was http://localhost:3000, so every link landed on a dead address (owner-side, since corrected)
signInBlocker.evidence: The owner completed a real sign-in on the durable branch origin. The provider records one live session and a sign-in timestamp on the real account, and the profile row created by the handle_new_user trigger is readable by that account and by nobody else.
